Date: 2028-05-18T09:22:00Z
Subject: [ALERT] gen-api latency wave — initial triage

Team —

Monitoring picked up a sustained P95/P99 spike across gen-api across multiple regions starting ~09:10 UTC. Initial observations:
- P95 up to 1.8s (baseline ~350ms), P99 up to 4.7s.
- Concurrency increased by ~37% from usual; throughput (tokens/s) down ~22% on affected model pool.
- Error budget not yet breached but tail latency impacting several high-traffic tenants (notably BrightCart).

Attached a snapshot from the alert window (alert-snapshot.png).

Immediate asks:
1) SRE: can we get a rapid canary to isolate whether scheduling/kernels or KV cache pressure is the driver?
2) Eng (runtime): any recent kernel/compilation changes pushed to prod in the last 24h?
3) Product/CS: we should prepare a short customer note for BrightCart pre-emptively; keep it factual and promise an ETA for normalization.

I'll start a triage bridge if we need it — thoughts?

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
SRE
Redwood Inference

--

From: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Date: 2028-05-18T09:35:00Z
Subject: Re: [ALERT] gen-api latency wave — initial triage

Thanks Jonas — saw the alert. Quick notes from the runtime side:
- No planned kernel/compile rollouts in last 24h on the gen-api pool; last automated kernel tweak was 48h ago.
- Hypothesis A: KV cache churn + longer decode loops causing backpressure in the batching loop.
- Hypothesis B: a small fraction of heavy seq-length sessions creating head-of-line blocking.

Immediate mitigations I can kick off (if SRE comfortable):
- Short rolling canary to route 8% of BrightCart traffic to a cold-start-friendly variant (smaller KV footprint).
- Temporarily lower max-batch-size from 64 to 32 for the affected pool to reduce latency tail.
- Enable prefix KV pinning for BrightCart queries for 30m.

Product asks / roadmap question for leadership: if we need to make routing-policy exceptions (burst capacity or model variant swap) for high-value tenants, what's the fastest approval path today? We should also consider adding a short-term toggle in Console to force-model-variant per-account for incidents like this.

Customer note draft (very short) below — please iterate:
"BrightCart — we detected a latency increase affecting some requests to gen-api starting ~09:10 UTC. Our engineers are actively investigating and have initiated mitigations; we expect normalization within 60–90 minutes. We'll update you with concrete remediation steps and any impact to your throughput by 10:45 UTC."

If SRE gives go, I'll start the canary and reduce batch size.

-Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: [ALERT] gen-api latency wave — initial triage

On it — quick technical notes and suggested playbook: 

Root-cause probes (running now):
- Heap/KV eviction rates per instance (in progress).
- Kernel execution time distribution for last 60m (in progress).
- Router queue depth + batching histogram per host.

Suggested mitigations (ordered):
1) Throttle new session admission for non-critical routes (reduce ingress by ~18%).
2) Route BrightCart to model-variant v2-alpha (smaller memory working set) as a temporary fallback. Requires routing-policy exception (see note).
3) Reduce max intra-shard batch window to 40ms (temporary), to limit latency amplification during bursty arrivals.

Operational ask for Product/Sales: BrightCart is in renewal discussion (BR-4721). If we enable model-variant fallback and/or temporary burst capacity, we'll likely need a formal exception & short note to Sales/Finance re: any credits. @marissa_cole — can you own the customer credit approval pathway while we stabilize?

Let me know if SRE can greenlight admission throttling + model swap; I'll push the routing change and monitor.

-karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: [ALERT] gen-api latency wave — initial triage

Thanks all — bridge opened (link in Jira INF-9654). Current status:
- I've approved a provisional routing-policy exception to route up to 10% of BrightCart traffic to v2-alpha and enabled admission throttling on non-critical routes. Exception expires in 90 minutes unless extended.
- Marcus: please run the canary and reduce batch size as proposed; SLO monitoring has been configured to auto-escalate if P99 > 5s for 10m.
- Karthik/Jonas: bring the KV eviction probes and kernel profiles into the bridge; we need a clear signal in 20m.

Customer-facing note (attached as BrightCart-cust-brief.md) — please use as the canonical customer message. Short preview below for threads:

"BrightCart Team —
We observed an increase in API latency beginning ~09:10 UTC that impacted request tail latency. Our engineers have applied routing and admission controls to mitigate the issue; we've also provisioned a temporary model variant to reduce memory pressure. We expect traffic to normalize within ~60–90 minutes. We will follow up with a technical postmortem and any credits if you experienced measurable impact to production throughput.

If you'd like a quick sync, we can join a call within the hour.

Sincerely,
Redwood Inference Ops"

Marissa — please coordinate customer credits & finance routing if the incident triggers a credit.

Evelyn Hart
SRE Manager
